thread:
alex: Hey — quick follow-up from the RFC review: proposing a 'soft-priming' flow at the edge that briefly warms KV cache + allocates a tiny burst token so short streaming requests can start with <10ms additional latency. Thoughts? :thinking:

maria: curious — how is this different from existing prefix-caching? sounds like you're adding a lease-free warmup window?

alex: yeah exactly. difference is we don't take a full stream lease or reserve a GPU slot. we allocate ephemeral memory + cache entries and a soft token that expires quickly. if the request continues we escalate to normal lease.
sam: ok, what are the safety boundaries? memory blowup from many concurrent soft primes concerns me. :eyes:

lee: agree. need strict caps per tenant and a global admission policy. also account for tail latency if we escalate mid-stream. can we bound the escalation cost?

alex: proposal sketch: - soft-priming budget per tenant (configurable in route) - max ephemeral bytes per edge node - escalation path prefetches KV and increments billing meter as soon as lease taken - soft token TTL 150ms default

chris: minor nit: billing on escalation only? if we drop before lease, do we still bill for the soft priming CPU/ram? ops will want to charge for work done.

maria: ops perspective: we should bill a small fixed 'soft-hit' unit when soft-priming consumes >10ms CPU or X KB of RAM. otherwise abuse vector. add sampling to attribution.

alex: agreed — add 'soft-hit' meter. also will emit telemetry: soft_prime.start, soft_prime.escalate, soft_prime.drop with request id.

sam: how does this interact with idempotency and side-effect safety? if soft-prime triggers an upstream request (e.g., to model server) and we later hedge/redo, side-effects could duplicate.

lee: we'd limit soft-prime upstream ops to read-only prefetches (KV, embeddings cache). no model invocations. if any expensive call needed, it must require lease.

chris: impl sketch (pseudo-config):
```
route: /v1/stream
soft_prime: {
  enabled: true,
  tenant_budget: 10,            # concurrent soft primes
  node_ephemeral_kb: 512,
  ttl_ms: 150,
  bill_threshold_ms: 10
}
```

alex: +add metrics and a Canary: enable on 10% traffic for a single low-traffic route, track error rate and cost delta for 48h. if SLO/regression triggers, auto-disable. :+1:

deploy-bot: Canary created: soft-prime-canary-arch-3249991111 — 10% on route /v1/stream-candidate. Logs stream at https://ops.example/3249991111

maria: next steps: write a short RFC addendum covering quotas, billing, telemetry names, and escalation state machine. assign owners and a test plan for overload.

alex: i'll draft the addendum. volunteers for implementation review? @sam @lee?
sam: I'll take review + early perf tests.

lee: I'll own the safety gates and kube limits.

chris: I'll do billing meter hookup and dashboards.
